Contribute

Help make useful research easier to find.

Authors can suggest their own work; community members can point to existing open resources. Every entry keeps its original ownership, citation and licence.

How contributions work

  1. Suggest a resource.
    Open a short structured request with the title, stable link, resource type and scientific scope.
  2. Check the essentials.
    We confirm that the link works and that access, licence, citation and provenance are described clearly.
  3. Publish the record.
    The resource is added to the catalogue with credit to the original authors and host.

What can be included?

Datasets, trained models, benchmarks, open software and practical tutorials connected to sprays, atomisation, interfaces, dispersed flows and related multiphase systems.

Suggest a resource on GitHubThe public submission form will open with the GitHub launch.

Minimum information

A catalogue entry should provide a stable title and URL, authors or maintaining organisation, a short scientific description, resource type, relevant flow class, access conditions, licence and preferred citation. Dataset records should also describe variables, formats, scale and known limitations.

Review principles

Inclusion means that a resource is relevant and sufficiently documented; it is not an endorsement of its scientific conclusions. Records should distinguish measured, simulated and derived data, and should state important restrictions rather than hiding them.

Contributions remain credited to their original creators.
